## Purpose
The HTTP API for workflow executions, modelled on Mistral's Workflow Executions API so the frontend can be written against that documented contract. It covers listing, detail, steps, history, traces, logs, live SSE, signals, queries and updates, cancel, terminate, reset and per-workflow metrics. Local DAG-engine runs and Mistral-hosted runs are merged.

## Responsibilities
| Endpoint | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /workflows/executions?workflow_identifier&status&search&user_id&page_size(1–200, 50)&next_page_token` | `exec_service.list_runs(...)`: Mistral and local runs merged |
| `POST /workflows/executions/cancel` and `/terminate` | batch control, body `{execution_ids}`; an empty list gets 422 |
| `GET /workflows/executions/{id}?with_steps=true` | `ExecutionDetail` from Mistral or the local store; 404 if unknown |
| `GET .../{id}/steps?include_internal=false` | progress steps; with no trace events, falls back to the full detail, which also tells an unknown id (404) from a run with no steps |
| `GET .../{id}/history?decode_payloads=true` | raw event history, the source of the `event_id` a reset targets |
| `GET .../{id}/trace/info` | whether trace data exists; never fails, answering `{available: false, detail}` when there is none |
| `GET .../{id}/trace/summary`, `/trace/events?merge_same_id_events&include_internal_events`, `/trace/otel` | trace views; the otel one is for export into an APM tool |
| `GET .../{id}/logs?limit(≤5000, 500)&since=0` | pollable logs; on failure returns empty logs with `next_seq: since` and `source: "none"` |
| `GET .../{id}/stream` | SSE events `execution_update`, `workflow_event`, `ping`, `error`, `done`; the client treats `done` as the close signal |
| `POST .../{id}/signals` | body `InvocationRequest{name or signal_name, input or payload}`; the handler defaults to `user_message`, which the execution console's chat uses |
| `POST .../{id}/signal` | hidden alias kept for older clients |
| `POST .../{id}/queries` and `/updates` | the handler name is required (422 "A handler 'name' is required.") |
| `POST .../{id}/cancel` | graceful: cleanup handlers still run |
| `POST .../{id}/terminate` | hard stop with no cleanup |
| `POST .../{id}/reset` | `{event_id, reason, exclude_signals, exclude_updates}` |
| `GET /workflows/{name}/metrics?start_time&end_time` | run counts, success/error split, latency and retry rate; on failure the fields are null with `available: false` |

## Key elements
- **`_sse(event, data)`** serialises with `json.dumps(default=str)` and repeats `data: ` on every line.
- **`_http_error(e, what)`** maps SDK failures to statuses:
  - text containing "404" or "not found" becomes 404 "<what> not found.";
  - "409" or "already" becomes 409;
  - anything else becomes 502 "<what> failed: <e>".
- **On a stream failure**, `_generate` yields an `error` event and then `done {status: "FAILED"}`.

## Control flow
None. The route is a thin layer over `services/workflow_engine/executions.py`.

## Data, state and side effects
Calls the Mistral Workflows API and reads the local execution store.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- `main.py` must include this router before `routes/workflows.py`.
- Route policy: GET needs workflows.view; POST needs workflows.run.
- Used by the frontend execution console and runs pages.

## Error handling and edge cases
See the table and Key elements.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Literal batch routes must be declared before `/{execution_id}`**, or FastAPI reads "cancel" as an id.
- **`signal_name` and `payload` are accepted as aliases** for `name` and `input`, so clients built against the older API keep working.
